items.titleEn: Intel stock plunges 17% after weak Q4 forecast overshadows AI growth
items.summaryEn: Buy AMD. If Intel’s PC and production issues persist, OEMs and PC supply chains keep shifting share toward competitors. AMD is the cleanest beneficiary of Intel’s client-computing stumble while the broader AI/data-center buildout continues. The setup is simple: Intel’s guidance shock signals share pressure in PCs, and AMD’s platform momentum should translate into higher unit demand and better mix. Key Risk: PC demand doesn’t just slow—it collapses across the whole market, hurting AMD’s volumes and forcing margin compression. Sell INTC. The stock got a big earnings beat, but the market is punishing the forward view: Q4 revenue $15–$16B vs $17.3B expected and EPS 25c vs 45c. The thesis is that PC weakness is worsening faster than Intel modeled (memory-price impact “sooner and deeper”), and the Israel facility disruption adds real near-term supply risk. AI/data-center growth can’t offset a client-computing slowdown when guidance is the problem.

items.titleEn: Oracle stock falls 4%: why experts aren't bothered
items.summaryEn: Buy Oracle (ORCL). The news is a clear step-up in free-cash-flow timing: positive FCF expected in 2H FY2028 (~12 months earlier), with capex peaking in FY2027–28 then stepping down in FY2029. That improves the odds Oracle funds AI infrastructure internally instead of repeatedly tapping capital markets. Add the higher pricing on 5-year contracts (~$16B per GW vs ~$10B) and management’s ~28% return on invested capital—this supports margin durability through the ramp. Key Risk: AI infrastructure delivery slips (power/permitting/labor), delaying the ~10GW ramp and pushing FCF positivity back out. Buy data-center power/utility exposure tied to new AI capacity buildouts: NextEra Energy (NEE). Oracle’s plan to add ~10GW of AI infrastructure capacity by FY2028 implies sustained demand for power generation and grid upgrades. Second-order effect: even if Oracle’s sites face timing risk, the power build and interconnection work tends to be longer-cycle and less reversible, supporting utility earnings visibility.
